results.corrected_title: Google widens Gemini 4 Argon access to the paid API, enterprises and AI Pro/Ultra subscribers
results.corrected_summary: On 13 October 2026 Google widened access to Gemini 4 Argon. The model was announced on 30 September for a limited group, mainly cyber defenders in the Fairwind Program. It is now on the paid Gemini API tier in AI Studio, in Gemini for business, in Google Antigravity, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Introductory pricing is $2/$10 per million input/output tokens until 30 November 2026, then $4/$20. Google says the model ranks #1 on the Vals Index and scores 87% on ERQA, and the Gemini app gets a tasks mode and connections to more than 40 apps.
key_facts: Pricing: $2 input / $10 output per million tokens (cached input 95% off) until 30 Nov 2026, then $4 / $20
Available on the paid Gemini API tier (AI Studio, Android Studio), in Gemini for business, in Antigravity, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode for AI Pro/Ultra; 1M-token limit via the API
Google's own claims: #1 on the Vals Index, 87% on ERQA, 0.7% attack success on the Gray Swan indirect prompt injection benchmark
Gemini app adds a tasks mode and connections to 40+ apps (Instacart, OpenTable, Adobe, Shopify); Antigravity is built into the macOS app
Fairwind Program expands to hundreds of additional partners; 10,000 scientists can get Antigravity's highest usage tier free for 6 months (subject to eligibility and selection)
Earlier limited launch on 2026-09-30, so 13 Oct is the new development
results.issues: The candidate's claims check out against Google's primary blog posts. The Sept 30 tester-only launch date comes from secondary search results only, not from a Google page I opened. The benchmark rankings are Google's own claims. I did not open the 9to5Google URL. 'Generally available' overstates it: access is still tiered (paid API, Pro/Ultra), not free for all users.

results.corrected_title: Meta releases open-weights Muse Spark Open (816B total, 42B active parameters)
results.corrected_summary: On 15 October 2026 Meta released Muse Spark Open, a natively multimodal open-weights model with 816B total and 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. The weights are on Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models, and hosted APIs include Baseten, Fireworks, Groq, OpenRouter and Together AI. It is released under the Muse Model License, which has limited commercial terms, so it is open-weight but not open source. Meta says it can run locally on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios using MLX.
key_facts: Weights on Hugging Face, SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Microsoft Foundry
Muse Model License with limited commercial terms (not an OSI open-source license)
Runs on two 512 GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX, per Meta
results.issues: The 'aimed at coding and agents' framing is loosely supported. Secondary sources say it matches Chinese models on agentic tasks but not on coding, and the benchmarks are vendor-reported. The model card lists at least 700 GB of VRAM (NVFP4) for GPU deployment.

results.corrected_title: Meta launches agentic models Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
results.corrected_summary: On 12 October 2026 Meta Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, which Meta calls its most capable models for agentic tasks. They introduce 'Active Memory' (keeping context across conversations) and 'Active Focus' (sustained work toward goals). Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while Wonder Full is for Muse Code subscribers only. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, Wonder scores 52 and Wonder Full 56, against 48 for Muse Spark 1.3.
key_facts: Active Memory and Active Focus features
Muse Wonder: Meta Model API and Muse Code; Wonder Full: Muse Code subscribers only; coming to the Muse app for subscribers first
AA Intelligence Index v4.3 (max reasoning): Wonder 52, Wonder Full 56, Muse Spark 1.3 48
Meta claims Wonder Full ranks 2nd on the index, 2 points behind Claude Opus 5.5
results.issues: The CNBC URL returned 403 and could not be checked. The fetched text of Meta's blog had no benchmark numbers (they appear to be in charts), so the AA Index scores come from TestingCatalog only. The Meta blog's publication date did not appear in the fetched text; the 12 Oct date comes from TestingCatalog and the CNBC URL path.
